question: Why does a truly random playlist so often play two songs by the same artist back to back?
answer: Because real randomness clumps. Shuffle 100 songs by 10 artists and each next song has about a one-in-ten chance of sharing the artist, so roughly nine back-to-back pairs are expected. Listeners hear a pattern and suspect the machine. Spotify changed its shuffle in 2014 to spread artists out: less random, so it felt more random.
move: Expect chance to clump; evenly spread results are the suspicious ones.
ask: Which streak of bad luck in my life did I read as a pattern when it was just chance clumping?
reference: Falk & Konold, Making sense of randomness: implicit encoding as a basis for judgment, Psychological Review 104:301–318, 1997
